note: No statewide ballot measures are on the November 3, 2026 Texas ballot. The Governor's proclamation for the general election orders it only 'for the purpose of electing state and district officers, members of the Texas Legislature, and members of the United States Congress' (https://www.sos.texas.gov/elections/forms/proclamation-general-election-2026.pdf). The Secretary of State's 2026 sample ballot (https://www.sos.texas.gov/elections/forms/2026-sample-ballot.pdf) lists only candidate races and no propositions. The Legislative Reference Library's constitutional amendment election list (https://lrl.texas.gov/legis/ConstAmends/electiondates.cfm) ends at Nov 4, 2025, and its amendment database has no proposals from any 89th Legislature called session. Texas constitutional amendment elections are held in odd-numbered years after the regular session; the 17 propositions from the 89th Legislature were voted on Nov 4, 2025. Read 2026-11-03. The SOS page https://www.sos.texas.gov/elections/voter/2026-important-election-dates.shtml returned HTTP 403 and was not used.
